transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Recorded by Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (Fairhaven - Head of Cloud), Maya Lin (Fairhaven - CISO), Jorge Alvarez (Fairhaven - Platform Eng)

Summary:
Fairhaven Bank is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted and private deployment options. Primary concerns: EU data residency (GDPR) for EU customers, HIPAA for a small healthcare vertical they support, strict logging/audit controls (logs not allowed to contain PII), and the ability to run Private (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM integration. They requested SOC2/ISO artifacts, a technical deep dive on Private deployment networking, and a pricing comparison.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday — appreciate it. We're here to talk through data residency, compliance, the Hosted versus Dedicated versus Private tradeoffs. Priya and I will run through the technical pieces and then take questions.
[00:15] Tom Reynolds: Hi, Tom here. Quick note — our compliance team is particularly worried about logs and egress, and we also need to understand any EU processing implications. We're US-headquartered but have customers in EU and UK.
[00:28] Maya Lin: Maya from InfoSec. We'll need to validate SOC2 and have answers on encryption, KMS, and if anything goes to third-party systems. Also HIPAA - some of our partners submit PHI so we need to know if Redwood can be configured for HIPAA-safe handling.
[00:42] Priya Shah: Great, thanks. Quick intro — I'm Priya, I work on infra and architecture at Redwood. We support three deployment modes: Hosted API (fast onboarding), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). Each has different guarantees around data residency and log access.
[01:05] Alex Morgan: I'll start with the high-level. Hosted is easiest but by default it routes to our multi-region hosted platform; you can pin region to US-only for data residency but EU processing for EU customers would need EU region pinning. Dedicated gives you isolated capacity and better SLAs. Private gives you full control — customer VPC or even on-prem.
[01:30] Jorge Alvarez: For Private, is there an option for customer-managed KMS? We need HSM-backed keys for some workflows.
[01:36] Priya Shah: Yes, for Private deployments we offer KMS integrations — we can integrate with AWS KMS, Cloud HSM, and customer HSM via KMIP in on-prem setups. For Dedicated we can also integrate with customer KMS with restrictions. Hosted uses our managed KMS by default but you can request CMK for enterprise contracts.
[01:58] Maya Lin: What about logs? We cannot have logs that contain PII or persistent KV caches storing user input. Does Redwood retain prompt/response logs by default?
[02:10] Priya Shah: By default we retain minimal logs for debugging and billing in Hosted; however, for enterprise we can disable retention of prompts, or redact and truncate logs. We also have request-level controls to avoid writing user inputs to long-term storage. For Private, logs remain within your VPC and you control storage and retention policies. Note: some metrics for performance are still collected but can be anonymized.
[02:40] Tom Reynolds: Can you promise that logs will never leave the US region if we pin to us-east? We need EU customer data to stay in EU regions only.
[02:49] Alex Morgan: Short answer: we can pin and set routing policy so requests for EU customers are processed in EU region. For EU-only customers we recommend Private or Dedicated with EU capacity. Hosted US-only pinning restricts routing to US regions, but you'll need to ensure clients are directing EU-customer traffic correctly. We'll put that routing policy detail in the follow-up doc.
[03:10] Maya Lin: GDPR-wise we need a data processing agreement and clarity on subprocessors. Do you have a DPA and list of subprocessors?
[03:18] Alex Morgan: Yes, we have a standard DPA and we maintain a subprocessors list; I'll include those in the security pack. We also support Data Subject Requests handling workflows — we'll outline responsibilities.
[03:30] Jorge Alvarez: On the technical side, if we use Hosted but want to minimize PII retention, can we run with prefix caching disabled? We read about KV cache/ prefix cache — not sure the exact term.
[03:40] Priya Shah: Sure — prefix/KV caching is configurable. You can disable persistent KV caches at request level; there's a tradeoff with latency and cost. Our Redwood runtime supports automatic caching and you can opt out per-route or per-API-key. We'll show config snippets.
[04:00] Tom Reynolds: About HIPAA — can Redwood be used for PHI? Does Redwood sign a BAA?
[04:06] Alex Morgan: We have customers who use Redwood under a BAA; for Hosted we'd need to scope the service and ensure PHI is only processed in HIPAA compliant configs. For stricter needs we usually recommend Private so PHI never leaves customer control. I'll flag legal to confirm specifics and include sample BAA language.
[04:28] Maya Lin: Encryption at rest/in transit — is everything TLS 1.2/1.3, and is disk-level encryption customer-managed in Dedicated/Private?
[04:38] Priya Shah: Yes, TLS 1.2+ enforced. For Dedicated and Private you can configure customer-managed encryption keys for disk and object storage. Hosted uses our managed encryption; for enterprise we offer CMKs.
[04:52] Jorge Alvarez: Any constraints on embeddings or persistent vector stores? Some of our ML pipelines store embeddings of customer data — need to ensure residency and retention.
[05:00] Priya Shah: We provide managed embeddings service; you can choose to store vectors in your VPC in Private mode or in our managed store with region pinning. For sensitive data we recommend hosting vectors in Private or Dedicated with your own storage.
[05:20] Tom Reynolds: For audit logs, we need tamper-evident logs and integration with our SIEM (Splunk). Do you stream logs to customer SIEM or do customers pull them?
[05:30] Priya Shah: We support log forwarding to customer SIEMs via syslog/S3 push or direct SIEM connectors. For Private, logs are inside your network and you control collection. For Hosted we can forward audit logs to your S3 in the same region — we'll include an example connector for Splunk.
[05:52] Alex Morgan: Quick note — some customers ask about function/tool calling and streaming traces; those traces may contain structured outputs. We can redact or strip those before storage.
[06:05] Maya Lin: Regarding contractual terms — SLA and data breach notification timelines? We need 24-48 hour notification for incidents and an uptime SLA.
[06:15] Alex Morgan: We have SLA tiers: Hosted has best-effort (but we provide uptime numbers for standard tiers), Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency, Private can be contractually defined. Incident response/notification timelines are in our enterprise agreements — I'll share the SLA matrix.
[06:36] Jorge Alvarez: If we do a Private deployment on AWS in our VPC, what's the deployment footprint? How many GPUs, are there pre-built AMIs?
[06:44] Priya Shah: For Private on AWS we provide an AMI and Terraform modules; footprint depends on expected QPS. We typically provide recommended cluster configs (GPUs, node types) and can help size. We also provide a guide for autoscaling and bursting to Redwood Dedicated if you want hybrid.
[07:10] Tom Reynolds: We have a question on data deletion — if a user requests deletion under GDPR, what's the process to delete logs and cached KV for that user?
[07:20] Priya Shah: We support deletion APIs and retention policies. For Hosted, we can delete all associated prompt logs and cached KV on request, and for Dedicated/Private you control data stores so you can delete directly. We'll document the deletion API and example workflows.
[07:40] Maya Lin: Are there any known issues with model weights or derivative data being included in exports? I.e., model updates that might memorize PII — we need mitigation and evals.
[07:52] Priya Shah: We run quality/regression checks and have eval hooks for prompt sets. For memorization concerns we can help set up guardrails and filters. For highly regulated PII we recommend Private and additional redaction before storage.
[08:10] Alex Morgan: Let's surface cost tradeoffs quickly — Hosted is cheapest to start, Dedicated is mid-range with committed capacity, Private is highest but gives full isolation. We can run a cost-per-1M-tokens estimate for each option.
[08:28] Tom Reynolds: For trials, can we run a US-only Hosted trial to validate function and then move to Private for EU-residency?
[08:35] Alex Morgan: Yes, common pattern. We'll set up a trial in us-east for initial testing and plan a follow-up for Private in EU. We'll include recommended sequence in the follow-up doc.
[08:50] Maya Lin: A couple more specifics — do you do annual penetration tests and provide reports?
[08:57] Alex Morgan: Yes, we do annual pentests and we can share executive summaries; full reports are carefully controlled under NDA.
[09:08] Jorge Alvarez: On the networking side, any restrictions for egress to external APIs from the model runtime? For example, some of our apps call out to internal KYC services.
[09:18] Priya Shah: Private mode allows you to control outbound access; you can lock down egress via VPC rules and NAT. Hosted has egress but we can restrict or whitelist destinations under enterprise agreements.
[09:36] Tom Reynolds: Do you have customers in banking doing similar things? Any references?
[09:43] Alex Morgan: We have several regional banks and financial services customers using Dedicated/Private for compliance. I'll share anonymized references in the pack.
[09:54] Maya Lin: Okay, one more — retention windows for debug logs vs audit logs. We only want short debug retention (7-14 days) and audit logs longer (7 years) but audit logs must be redacted. Is that possible?
[10:06] Priya Shah: Yes — retention is configurable per-log type. Audit logs can be stored to your S3 with immutability settings if required; debug logs can be truncated automatically. We'll show examples.
[10:22] Jorge Alvarez: About model routing — can we route by customer region or by token type? For instance, EU customers always to EU models, US to US.
[10:30] Alex Morgan: Yes, our smart routing rules allow routing by geolocation, API-key, or tenant. You can define fallbacks too.
[10:42] Maya Lin: Any regulatory concerns about chain-of-custody for logs if an auditor requests full trace?
[10:50] Priya Shah: We can provide signed, timestamped audit exports and show the provenance. For Private, chain-of-custody is fully within your control. For Hosted we provide provable exports and signing on request.
[11:05] Tom Reynolds: Great. Can you also capture in writing any limitations of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private so our legal team can review?
[11:12] Alex Morgan: Yes — we'll include a short comparison table in the follow-up.
[11:18] Maya Lin: We'll need to involve procurement and legal soon. Timeline wise, we're aiming for a decision by end of Q3 — so late Sep. We may need a pilot beforehand.
[11:28] Alex Morgan: Sounds good. We'll align next steps. Priya, anything to add?
[11:33] Priya Shah: I'll add network diagrams and sample config for redaction flags and KMS integration. Also will include an example of disabling KV cache and a retention policy snippet.
[11:45] Jorge Alvarez: If we wanted to try Dedicated rather than Private first, are there deployment templates? How fast can Dedicated capacity be provisioned?
[11:52] Alex Morgan: Dedicated provisioning typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on region and capacity. Private can take longer for on-prem. We'll put expected timelines in the doc.
[12:05] Tom Reynolds: Ok, last question — how do you handle subpoenas or legal holds? If a regulator asks for data, what's the workflow?
[12:13] Alex Morgan: We have a legal process; for Hosted we respond per the DPA and legal agreements. For Dedicated/Private customers, we follow contractual obligations and will coordinate with your legal team. We'll include the general process in the pack.
[12:28] Maya Lin: Thanks. That covers most of it.
[12:32] Alex Morgan: Thanks all. We'll send the security pack and schedule the technical deep dive.
[12:38] Tom Reynolds: Appreciate it. We'll get sample retention requirements and the list of contacts to Jorge.

Outro / Closing notes:
- Alex to send DPA, subprocessors list, SOC2/ISO summaries, example BAA language, and SLA matrix.
- Priya to prepare Private deployment network diagram, KMS/HSM integration notes, and config snippets for disabling KV cache and log redaction.
- Customer to provide sample data patterns and retention rules.

Transcription notes: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KMS" rendered as "KMS", "KV cache" sometimes typed as "kay-vee cache"), minor speaker attribution issues.
